answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks through stake-weighted admission: each identity must lock real collateral before it earns a vote, so an unfunded fake account carries zero weight. To buy N extra votes an attacker must post N separate deposits, so the cost rises linearly with attack size instead of staying near zero. When a fake node double-signs or colludes, its stake is slashed, driving the expected payoff to its nadir. Honest agents keep collateral like a timber beam holds a roof; a forged identity is fragile as an opal and shatters when challenged.
